::api-operation{method="POST" path="/v1/businesses/{biz}/payment_intents"}
#docs
Creates the intent AND its first attempt; the response carries `attempt`, because the buyer’s challenge (`next_action`) belongs to that attempt.

**`purpose: payment`** — requires `payment_method` and a positive `amount_minor`. The customer comes from the payment method, so `customer` must be omitted.

**`purpose: setup`** — requires `customer`, and takes NO `payment_method` (the buyer supplies the instrument during the challenge) and NO amount (`amount_minor` must be omitted or 0). This is the zero-amount vaulting authorization; it was previously impossible to express over this API.

## Path parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `biz` | `string` | **yes** | Business id (biz_…) |

## Headers

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Idempotency-Key` | `string` | no | Safely retry writes — repeats return the original response. If a write FAILED after it had already taken effect, that failure is what repeats: the key is spent, and a new attempt needs a new key. |

## Body

The request body is **required**.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `purpose` | `string` | no | What the intent is for. `setup` is a zero-amount authorization that vaults an instrument. One of `payment`, `setup`. Defaults to `"payment"`. |
| `payment_method` | `string` | no | `payment` only — a setup intent has nothing vaulted yet to authorize. |
| `customer` | `string` | no | `setup` only — for a `payment` intent the customer comes from the payment method. |
| `amount_minor` | `integer` | no | Integer minor units, at most 10^12. Positive for `payment`; omitted or 0 for `setup`. |
| `currency` | `string` | **yes** | The business's default currency or one on its currency list, or the currency of the `invoice` or `subscription` named. Any other is a 400. |
| `invoice` | `string` | no | Context link stored on the intent. |
| `subscription` | `string` | no | Context link stored on the intent. |
| `return_url` | `string` | no | Where the gateway returns the buyer after a redirect challenge. |
| `cancel_url` | `string` | no | Where to send the customer if they cancel. |
| `method_types` | `array of string` | no | Instruments the buyer may use, in our canonical vocabulary (`card`, `us_bank_account`, `upi`, …). |
| `session` | `string` | no | An off_session buyer cannot complete a challenge. One of `on_session`, `off_session`. |
| `max_amount_minor` | `integer` | no | `setup` only — the per-debit ceiling of the mandate this intent registers, in minor units of `currency`. Mandate rails (RazorPay e-mandate/UPI/card) demand an upper bound at registration and enforce it at debit time, so omitting it lets the gateway apply its own default cap. It is stored on the intent, so a retry re-registers with the same ceiling. Rejected for `purpose: payment`, which registers no mandate. |
| `gateway_account` | `string` | no | Pin the intent to this gateway account instead of routing. It must be this business's, active, in its mode, and able to take the currency and method. |

## Response

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `object` | `string` | The object type; always `payment_intent`. One of `payment_intent`. |
| `id` | `string` | The payment intent's id (pi_…). |
| `status` | `string` | `voided` is set by the void route alongside `voided_at`. One of `inited`, `in_progress`, `authorized`, `consumed`, `expired`, `voided`. |
| `purpose` | `string` | Whether the intent takes a payment or saves a payment method. One of `payment`, `setup`. |
| `amount_minor` | `integer` | Always 0 for a `setup` intent. |
| `max_amount_minor` | `integer` | The mandate ceiling this `setup` intent registered with, and what a retry re-registers with. Null for `payment` intents. |
| `currency` | `string` | The payment intent's currency (ISO-4217 code). |
| `attempt_count` | `integer` | Payment attempts — how many times this intent has been tried at the gateway. |
| `last_attempt_status` | `string` | Status of the NEWEST attempt. `status` above cannot express a refusal — there is no `failed` intent status, because a declined authorization leaves the intent OPEN so it can be retried — so this is what distinguishes a declined intent from one the buyer is still working through. `null` means no attempt has been made yet. One of `inited`, `requires_action`, `authorized`, `consumed`, `failed`, `voided`. |
| `next_action` | `object` | How the buyer completes the challenge, when one is outstanding. |
| `expires_at` | `string · ISO-8601` | When the intent expires (ISO-8601 UTC). |
| `voided_at` | `string · ISO-8601` | When the intent was voided (ISO-8601 UTC), or null. |
| `created_at` | `string · ISO-8601` | When the payment intent was created (ISO-8601 UTC). |
| `resource_version` | `integer` | A number that goes up on every change. |
| `attempt` | `object` | The most recent attempt. |

## Status codes

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `201` | Created |
| `400` | Invalid purpose/amount/payment-method combination, a currency the business does not bill in, a gateway refusal, or no eligible gateway |
| `404` | No such business |
| `409` | Idempotency-Key conflict — the key is already in flight, or was reused with a different request payload. |

#request
```bash [Request]
curl -X POST "$TMBILLING_URL/v1/businesses/biz_XXXXXXXXXXXX01/payment_intents" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TMBILLING_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "amount_minor": 2900,
    "currency": "USD"
  }'
```
